planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into gritty, well-drained soil; avoid low, wet spots since it is prone to rot in poorly drained or consistently soggy soil.

directions: Plant divisions in spring into gritty, well-drained soil; the soft gray-woolly foliage spreads into a dense low mat that works well tucked between flagstones or cascading over the edge of a raised bed. Small blue or pink-veined flowers smother the foliage in mid-spring, and the mat tolerates being lightly walked on once it has filled in. It handles heat and drought well but is prone to rot in poorly drained or consistently soggy soil, so avoid low, wet spots.

planting.note: Set rooted divisions six to ten inches apart in spring into well-drained soil; water regularly the first season to establish.

directions: Set rooted divisions six to ten inches apart in spring into well-drained soil; the small rounded succulent leaves form a dense low carpet that fills quickly between pavers and along path edges. It tolerates more shade than most stonecrops, making it useful where a sun-loving sedum would scorch, and small yellow star flowers appear in summer. Water regularly the first season to establish, after which it needs little beyond occasional deep watering during extended drought.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Install plugs eight to twelve inches apart in spring or fall; because it spreads by rhizomes it can be assertive in richer, moist soil, so give it a contained area.

directions: Install plugs eight to twelve inches apart in spring or fall; this rhizomatous North American native sedge spreads steadily to knit into a fine-textured, no-mow lawn substitute that can also be mowed occasionally to two or three inches for a tidier look. It tolerates a wider range of soil moisture than most meadow sedges, handling both summer drought and periodic heavier watering, which makes it versatile for converting turf areas in mixed-use yards. Because it spreads by rhizomes it can be assertive in richer, moist soil, so give it a contained area or expect to edge it back from adjoining beds.
